question_text: Which of the following is a limitation of a composite development index?

options.B: It is legally binding on states
options.C: It may conceal district disparities and depend on indicator weights

option_assessment.A: Incorrect: indices are calculated from indicators and datasets.
option_assessment.B: Incorrect: a statistical index is not inherently legally binding; this is not a universal legal attribute.
option_assessment.C: Correct: aggregation may obscure distribution; construction depends on indicator selection and weighting. UNDP's IHDI explicitly adjusts aggregate HDI for inequality.
option_assessment.D: Incorrect: descriptive index values do not by themselves establish causal attribution.

primary_sources.title: Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index
primary_sources.evidence: HDI dimension averages do not reflect the full distribution; IHDI adjusts for inequality.

primary_sources.title: Documentation and downloads
primary_sources.evidence: Composite indices have published technical methodologies, inputs and calculation rules.

limitations: UNDP documents demonstrate the general aggregation/inequality issue; they do not directly measure Telangana district disparities.
